source_spans.locator: Science 317, published pp.1351-1352, Abstract and opening: humans can pre-experience possible future events and use present reactions to anticipate hedonic consequences, including events not previously experienced in the same form

Science 317, published p.1352, Mechanisms of Prospection: stored and incoming information support a future-event representation; the representation elicits a present hedonic reaction that is used as an indicator of the later reaction

Science 317, published p.1352, Errors of Prospection / Figure 1: present and future hedonic states each depend on event representation/perception plus context; reliable prediction requires matched event influence and matched contextual influence across T1 and T2
Science 317, published pp.1352-1353, 'Simulations are unrepresentative': stored past episodes can be sampled unrepresentatively, producing over- or underestimation of a future recurrence

Science 317, published p.1353, 'Simulations are essentialized': omitted incidental features can materially change later experience; omission increases with temporal distance and can exaggerate predicted valence

Science 317, published p.1353, 'Simulations are abbreviated' / Figure 2: constructed representations overrepresent early moments, underrepresent adaptation, and can reverse the ordering of predicted versus later experienced mood

Science 317, published p.1354, 'Simulations are decontextualized': present and future contextual states often differ; failing to account for that difference distorts forecasts, while prompting consideration of future context improves accuracy

Science 317, published p.1354, Conclusion: future-event representations can elicit brief present hedonic reactions but are less rich, sustained, and contextualized than actual perception; the resulting reactions can therefore differ

institutions: Department of Psychology, University of Virginia

conditions: a person constructs a present representation of a possible future event and uses the present hedonic response to that representation to estimate a later hedonic response
the constructed representation can draw on stored information from earlier episodes but need not correspond to an event previously experienced in the same form

forecast reliability depends on how similarly the constructed representation and later perception influence hedonic state and on how similarly present and future contextual factors influence hedonic state
population: humans in the behavioral, neuropsychological, and neuroimaging literature reviewed by the source
task: construct or imagine a possible future event, register the present hedonic reaction it evokes, and estimate the hedonic reaction expected when the event later occurs
temporal_scope: T1 is the present construction-and-forecast period; T2 is the later event-experience period
greater temporal distance can increase omission of incidental features, and abbreviated representations can underrepresent adaptation that unfolds after event onset

nodes.description: information specifying or constraining a possible later event
stored information from earlier experiences that can supply components used to construct the possible later event
presently generated representation of a possible later event
bodily, environmental, and cognitive circumstances present during construction and forecasting at T1
pleasant or unpleasant reaction elicited in the present by the constructed representation together with current context
explicit estimate of the later pleasantness or unpleasantness expected if the event occurs
later perceptual encounter with the event at T2, if it occurs
bodily, environmental, and cognitive circumstances present when the event is later experienced at T2
pleasant or unpleasant state actually experienced when the event is later encountered
agreement between the estimated later hedonic response and the later experienced hedonic response
difference between the estimated and later experienced hedonic response
construction based disproportionately on unusual, recent, or otherwise non-typical stored episodes
omission of features that do not define the event but can materially affect its eventual hedonic impact
compression of a future event into a small set of moments weighted toward its beginning, thereby underrepresenting later adaptation
difference between context affecting present reaction at T1 and context affecting later experience at T2
delay between the present forecast and the possible future event

relations.description: available event information and stored experience can be combined into a present representation of a possible later event
the present hedonic reaction depends jointly on the constructed event representation and contextual influences at T1
the present hedonic reaction is used as an indicator for estimating the hedonic response expected at T2
the later experienced hedonic state depends jointly on the actual event as perceived and contextual influences at T2
a forecast is accurate to the extent that the estimated later hedonic response agrees with the response actually experienced
prediction error arises when the constructed event or present context influences T1 hedonic state differently from the later event or context at T2
using non-typical stored episodes changes the constructed representation and can produce systematic over- or underestimation of later experience
omitting features that later contribute to experience tends to exaggerate the predicted positivity of good events and negativity of bad events
omission of incidental features becomes more pronounced for more temporally distant events in the reviewed evidence
overweighting early moments and underrepresenting later adaptation can make predicted long-run hedonic impact more extreme than later experience
failing to account for contextual differences between T1 and T2 distorts the predicted later hedonic response
construction and forecast occur at T1 before the possible later perceptual encounter and realized hedonic response at T2
